newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Asian Dev Bank approves $3.0 billion loans, grants.
newsitem.headline: Asian Dev Bank approves $3.0 billion loans, grants.

text.p: The Asian Development Bank said on Friday it had approved a total of $3.0 billion in loans and grants in the first nine months of 1996 compared with $2.84 billion in the year-earlier period.
For the third quarter alone, loan approvals and grants amounted to $1.2 billion versus $2.05 billion in the 1995 period, according to the latest issue of the ADB Review.
About 24 loans were given to 13 developing member countries in the third quarter amounting to $1.16 billion.

The top five borrowers during the first three quarters were Indonesia at $641 million; Pakistan, $415 million; China, $482 million; Philippines, $318.4 million; and Nepal, $289.2 million, the ADB said.

On a sectoral basis, $1.02 billion of the loans approved during the nine-month period went to energy; transport and communications were the target of $719 million; social infrastructure, $527.6 million; agriculture, $436.5 million; and industry and nonfuel minerals, $80 million; finance, $25 million; and others, $67.2 million, the ADB said.
